name: Injected private menu mutation server-handler boundary
phase: Discovery and specification only; implementation requires separate authorization
purpose: Compose an already-created native Request adapter and the existing response mapper into one route-independent handler, without runtime acquisition, policy duplication or production activation.

discovery.M: FoodMenuMutationRequestBoundary.submit(envelope): Promise<FoodMenuMutationRequestResult>. createPrivateFoodMenuMutationRequestBoundary takes operationGate/workspace/expectedOrigin. It alone owns metadata policy, gate-before-body, bounded parsing, eight mutations and downstream workspace dispatch.
discovery.N: FoodMenuMutationRequestAdapter.submit(request: Request): Promise<FoodMenuMutationRequestResult>. createPrivateFoodMenuMutationRequestAdapter({ boundary }) synchronously returns a frozen adapter, captures boundary.submit with its receiver, returns fulfilled results by identity and sanitizes unexpected boundary failures. Body access is deferred until the authorized async generator advances.
discovery.O: createPrivateFoodMenuMutationResponse(result: FoodMenuMutationRequestResult): Response is synchronous. It owns all fifteen status mappings, fixed JSON projection and headers, and guards malformed results without accessing snapshot contents.
discovery.LJ: createPrivateFoodMenuOperationRuntimeFromServerContext accepts FoodPrivateMenuServerContextInput and returns FoodPrivateMenuOperationServerContextResult. Its success bundle is service/workspace/operationGate, with gate and service the same instance. Construction is request-scoped and I/O-free; later resolution reads sessions/identity. P must not repeat it.
discovery.I: acquirePrivateFoodMenuDatabaseFromEnvironment accepts generic environment and explicit canonical bindingName, structurally checks the chosen prepare/batch capability and returns it unchanged. Missing/malformed configuration uses configuration-unavailable with Food menu database configuration is unavailable. This is not an M/N mutation result.
discovery.K: FoodPrivateMenuOperationGate.runAuthorized authorizes fresh without repository calls, invokes the callback only if authorized, and sanitizes callback failure. The normal service mutation independently authorizes again. P delegates rather than introducing another gate.
discovery.precedents: createInsuranceQuoteRequestApi returns a route-independent async Request-to-Response function. Sesh HTTP handlers also use standard Request/Response. Insurance Astro endpoints use prerender=false and assemble trusted dependencies per invocation. Frozen submit/handle-style object capabilities match current food adapter/workspace conventions; P selects a frozen handle-only object to align with N while retaining Web-only execution.
discovery.food001: Food source inspection found no FOOD-001 Request-to-Response server-handler factory to reuse. D1FoodDraftRepository already implements the raw exact getProduct/getRecipe contract. FOOD-001 runtime composition deliberately exposes its authorized service rather than that repository. No production menu read-dependency assembly was found.
discovery.verificationScope: Committed source, types, specifications and test inspection only; no Request body read, Response construction, database operation or runtime activation performed during discovery. Runtime claims below are implementation test obligations.

selectedArchitecture.choice: A: inject an already-created FoodMenuMutationRequestAdapter; delegate Request to N and materialized result to O.

alternatives.B: Not selected: accepting M and constructing N is pure but repeats the existing explicit N assembly step and enlarges P's construction responsibility without a new required capability.
alternatives.C: Not selected: accepting gate/workspace/origin absorbs M construction and exposes policy dependencies P does not need.
alternatives.D: Not selected: server-context/runtime assembly introduces unrelated configuration, session and identity dependencies and unresolved production sources.
alternatives.E: A returned callable would match the insurance precedent, but the selected frozen handle-only object matches established food capability surfaces. No second callable alias is added.

selectedArchitecture.inputDefinition: export interface FoodMenuMutationServerHandlerInput { readonly adapter: FoodMenuMutationRequestAdapter; }
selectedArchitecture.handlerDefinition: export interface FoodMenuMutationServerHandler { handle(request: Request): Promise<Response>; }
selectedArchitecture.imports: Reuse FoodMenuMutationRequestAdapter from ./private-menu-mutation-request-adapter and FoodMenuMutationRequestResult from ./private-menu-mutation-request as types; import createPrivateFoodMenuMutationResponse directly from ./private-menu-mutation-response. No injected mapper, alternate adapter abstraction or additional runtime dependency.
selectedArchitecture.excludedInputs: No boundary, gate, workspace, runtime bundle, environment, database, repository, session, resolver, administrator, origin, HTTP configuration or full Astro context.

construction.validation: Require non-null/non-array object input and adapter and callable adapter.submit. Capture input.adapter and adapter.submit once, catching throwing property access. Invalid construction throws TypeError with exactly Private food menu mutation server handler configuration is unavailable. No new result/error code or HTTP response is produced during construction.
construction.purity: Synchronous structural checks only. Zero adapter submissions, authorization, caller resolution, session/clock/DB/FOOD-001/network/environment operations, request inspection or Response creation.
construction.output: Object.freeze({ handle }) with only the handle property. Do not expose the adapter or captured dependencies. Do not mutate/freeze caller-owned dependencies. Retain the captured submit method and invoke with its original adapter receiver, so method replacement after construction does not retarget the handler.

execution: handle(request) passes the exact original Request object unchanged to the captured adapter.submit.call(adapter, request) exactly once and awaits it.
Do not inspect any Request property, including method/headers/url/body/bodyUsed/signal. Do not parse, buffer, clone, tee, prevalidate, consume or retry it. N/M retain their full existing ordering.

Pass the exact fulfilled result by identity directly to createPrivateFoodMenuMutationResponse exactly once, without cloning, projecting, inspecting or retaining its payload. O alone validates and maps malformed results.
Return the exact Response instance returned by O unchanged. Do not rebuild, clone, serialize, inspect or change its body/status/headers. P has no status/header/JSON mapping table.

Catch only unexpected synchronous throw or async rejection from the captured adapter submission. Map it to a frozen materialized M-compatible { ok: false, error: { code: 'callback-failed', message: 'Private food menu operation could not be completed.' } } and pass that to O. No exception text or new taxonomy; no retry.

Do not put O invocation inside the adapter-failure catch. Standard Web Response availability is a server-runtime prerequisite; unexpected platform/mapper invocation failure propagates without retry or competing serializer. O already guards malformed input.

No logging, telemetry, private payload retention, reusable authorization token or configuration-unavailable mapping. Runtime configuration failures must be handled upstream in a separately specified assembly layer.
bodyLaziness: M rejects metadata before gate/body. K denies before invoking the lazy body callback. N owns reader creation and consumption only after authorization. P touches no body state. Tests must verify zero reader acquisition/read/cancel and no body/bodyUsed access for method/origin and all three denied access paths, while distinguishing independent source prefetch from handler-driven consumption. Normal workspace mutations still reauthorize through FOOD-002E after the gate; P supplies no inherited permission.
concurrency: All request, result and Response state is invocation-local. One handler may process concurrent independent Requests without shared readers, payloads, result slots or authorization decisions. This does not make a request-scoped J/L session resolver safe to share across different users: trusted upstream assembly must create separate runtime/M/N/P graphs per request/session. A shared synthetic or otherwise concurrency-safe injected N adapter may be tested with independent Requests; P adds no broader identity-lifetime guarantee.

authority.N: Sole native Request adaptation authority; P receives N rather than constructing it.
authority.M: Sole transport policy/parser/limits/dispatch/expectedOrigin authority. P neither sees expectedOrigin nor selects it.
authority.O: Sole HTTP Response projection/status/header/cache/CORS authority. Its Response is returned unchanged.
authority.KService: Gate and service own fresh authorization. No authorization behavior changes.
authority.runtime: L/J/I remain upstream runtime/composition/acquisition authorities. BindingName/admin/readDependencies/configuration-unavailable stay outside P.
authority.framework: Standard Web Request/Response only; no Astro APIContext/APIRoute, cloudflare:workers, globals, route exports or generated typing required.

futureRoute.status: Documentary only; do not create or register this path in P.
futureRoute.shape: A later separately approved thin APIRoute with prerender=false assembles trusted FoodPrivateMenuServerContextInput per request, calls createPrivateFoodMenuOperationRuntimeFromServerContext, handles configuration-unavailable outside P/O, constructs M from runtime.operationGate/runtime.workspace plus trusted expectedOrigin, constructs N({ boundary }), constructs P({ adapter }), and returns await handler.handle(context.request).
futureRoute.methods: Prefer an all-method Astro adapter so M remains POST rejection authority, rather than assuming a POST-only export verifies all methods. Actual framework routing, HEAD wire-body suppression, OPTIONS behavior, middleware and configuration-failure HTTP mapping require later integration tests/specification; none is implemented or claimed here.
futureRoute.sessionLifetime: Do not globally cache J/L request session/resolver graphs. River OS boolean authentication is not menu authorization.

exactReadDependencyGap.requiredResults: Promise<FoodDraftReadResult<FoodProductDraft>> and Promise<FoodDraftReadResult<FoodRecipeDraft>>, each raw found/not-found with exact requested ID/version and detached frozen snapshots; repository failures throw rather than service-envelope success.
exactReadDependencyGap.available: D1FoodDraftRepository has compatible raw exact reads and can supply bound narrow methods when constructed by a trusted internal caller. No new storage primitive is missing. FOOD-001 runtime instead exposes FoodPrivateDraftService or service/gate; its exact reads return FoodDraftServiceResult wrapping those raw results.
exactReadDependencyGap.missing: No production assembly currently selects/configures the FOOD-001 historical source and supplies its exact reads to J/L. The authorized FOOD-001 service is not directly assignable because of its ok/value/error envelope. A future dependency-composition specification must decide trusted repository-based internal reads versus authorized-service adaptation, explicitly preserve access failures/fail-closed behavior, bind receivers and avoid exposing raw repositories as public authorization bypasses. Do not silently unwrap failures into not-found, use latest reads or expose database/repository through P.
exactReadDependencyGap.scope: P cannot and must not resolve that policy/source decision. It is a prerequisite graph question, not another HTTP mapping layer.
